sections.title: Build regular past forms
body: Past tense tells about a finished time: igår, förra veckan or för tre år sedan. The verb has one past form for every person: jag jobbade, du jobbade, vi jobbade.

Four useful patterns are -ade, -de, -te and -dde. Group 1 keeps its -a and adds -de: jobba → jobbade. For group 2, remove the infinitive’s -a: ringa → ring → ringde. A group-2 stem ending in a voiceless sound (p, t, k, s or x) takes -te: köpa → köp → köpte. Short regular verbs such as bo and må add -dde: bodde, mådde.
Voiceless means your throat does not buzz when you say the sound. Compare s (no buzz) with z (buzz). The -te clue applies to group 2, not to every verb: prata is group 1 and becomes pratade.

examples.fi: Han läste en bok förra veckan.
examples.en: He read a book last week.

examples.fi: Jag bodde i Stockholm för fyra år sedan.
examples.en: I lived in Stockholm four years ago.

sections.memoryTip: One past verb works with every person. No extra ending for he, she or we.
sections.tryIt: Say what you did yesterday with jobbade, ringde, köpte or bodde.

activity.label: Ending sort
activity.title: Which regular ending do you hear?
activity.instructions: Sort each past form by its ending, then say the complete pair.

items.why: jobba belongs to group 1: add -de to the full infinitive, giving -ade.
ring ends in a voiced sound: add -de.
köp ends in the voiceless p sound: add -te.
bo has a long vowel: add -dde.

activity.summary: The stem sound helps choose -de or -te; the first and third patterns are easiest to learn as groups.

sections.title: Learn the common irregular pairs
body: Some very common verbs do not follow these regular ending patterns. Learn each present–past pair as one small chunk. The textbook groups them together under strong verbs; more generally, call them irregular verbs.
Start with forms that make a whole day possible: är–var, har–hade, går–gick, äter–åt, dricker–drack and sover–sov. Inte still comes after the first verb: Jag hade inte tid.

examples.fi: Vi åt middag och drack kaffe.
examples.en: We ate dinner and drank coffee.

sections.memoryTip: Say the pair with rhythm: går–gick, äter–åt, dricker–drack, sover–sov.
sections.tryIt: Cover the past column and recall all six forms.

sections.title: React to good news
body: A past story is also a conversation. React first, then ask one follow-up question. Vilka fantastiska nyheter! is an enthusiastic reaction. Grattis! means congratulations.
Stolt över dig is proud of you. Hur var det? asks for a past description. Vad gjorde du? asks what somebody did.

examples.en: I am so proud of you.

sections.title: Go home, then be at home
body: Hem shows direction: movement toward home. Hemma shows location: you are already there. English often says “home” for both, so notice the Swedish verb.
The same direction–location idea appears in ut–ute, in–inne, upp–uppe and ner–nere. Learn hem and hemma first because they are useful in every diary.

examples.en: In the evening I was at home.

examples.fi: Jag måste gå ut. Jag är ute nu.
examples.en: I must go out. I am outside now.

sections.memoryTip: A moving verb chooses hem. Vara chooses hemma.

pronunciation.text: jobbade, ringde, köpte, bodde. Var, hade, gick, åt, drack, sov. Jag gick hem. Jag var hemma.
pronunciation.tip: Keep the final -de or -te audible. In gick, the g sounds like English y. Contrast short hem with two-syllable hemma.

listening.text: Igår vaknade Alex klockan sju. Han åt frukost och drack kaffe. Sedan gick han till jobbet. På jobbet pratade han med Elin och skrev många meddelanden. Efter jobbet köpte han mat. Han gick hem klockan sex och lagade soppa. På kvällen pluggade han svenska, såg en kort film och ringde en vän. Han var trött och sov bra.

reading_passage.text:
Dagbok
Igår hade Maja en mycket bra dag. Hon vaknade tidigt och åt frukost hemma. Sedan gick hon till skolan. Där skrev hon ett prov. Provet var svårt, men Maja kunde svara på frågorna. Efter skolan träffade hon Elin på ett kafé. Maja berättade de fantastiska nyheterna: hon klarade provet. De drack kaffe och pratade om en fest. Sedan gick Maja hem. Hemma åt hon middag, skickade en inbjudan och sov bra.

route.expectedOutput: Tell Elin about yesterday in six past-tense lines, then write a 35–60-word diary entry.
route.transferPrompt: Change one detail: tell the same day with a different meal, place or evening activity.

successChecks: Move from morning to evening in a clear order.
Use at least four correct past-tense verbs.
Include one regular and one irregular past form.
Use hem for movement or hemma for location correctly.

assignment.title: Episode 6 mission: Yesterday
assignment.instructions:
CORE: Tell Elin what you did yesterday in six lines, from morning to evening. Use at least four past verbs.

WRITING: Start your diary with five to seven sentences about yesterday.

DAILY: Continue the diary for 5–10 minutes every day, as your teacher asked.

RETURN: Tomorrow, retell the day without looking.
assignment.model: Igår vaknade jag klockan sju och åt frukost. Sedan gick jag till jobbet. På dagen jobbade jag mycket och pratade med en kollega. Efter jobbet köpte jag mat. Jag gick hem klockan sex. På kvällen åt jag middag och pluggade svenska.

takeaways: Use one past form for every person: jag jobbade, hon jobbade, vi jobbade.
Learn frequent irregular verbs as pairs: är–var, går–gick, äter–åt, dricker–drack, sover–sov.
Hem is a direction; hemma is a location. React to news before asking what happened.
